course.title: Arabic for Beginners
course.tagline: Read and speak Arabic from zero: letters, words and simple sentences.

days.title: Say marhaba and hello
days.goal: Greet people in Arabic and say goodbye.

video.title: Arabic for Beginners — Lesson 1

steps: Watch today's video and repeat every example of greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama out loud as you hear it.
Practise greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama aloud for 10 minutes, slowly first, then at normal speed.
Write down five of your own examples using greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama.
Record yourself practising greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama and listen back, fixing any mistakes you hear.
Use greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama in a real exchange today — with a friend, family member or language partner.
days.task: Say marhaba, as-salamu alaykum and ma'a as-salama out loud five times each.
days.challenge: Greet someone in Arabic today, even by message.

quiz.q: What does 'marhaba' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Marhaba' means hello. 'As-salamu alaykum' is a warm greeting that means 'peace be upon you.'

quiz.q: Which of these is the goal of today's lesson?
options: Hold a short greeting chat in Arabic.
Greet people in Arabic and say goodbye.
Name foods and say what you like.
Ask where a place is in Arabic.
quiz.explain: Today's lesson is about Say marhaba and hello — its goal is: Greet people in Arabic and say goodbye.

quiz.q: Which of these did today's lesson focus on?
options: the Arabic alphabet: 28 letters, written right to left
saying where you are from: Ana min... / Askunu fi...
describing people: tawil, qasir, latif, marih
greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama
quiz.explain: Today's focus was greetings: marhaba, as-salamu alaykum, ma'a as-salama.
